correctness.rationale: An affine zero mode gives a two-by-two boundary system whose determinant vanishes exactly when \(\lambda_0+\lambda_\ell-\lambda_0\lambda_\ell\ell=0\), and then the kernel is one-dimensional. Since both Robin parameters are nonzero, the zero-energy scattering matrix is \(-I_2\), giving scattering multiplicity one. Expanding the exact secular function gives a linear coefficient proportional to \(\ell-\lambda_0^{-1}-\lambda_\ell^{-1}\); on resonance the cubic coefficient is nonzero because \(\lambda_0^{-3}+\lambda_\ell^{-3}=\ell(\lambda_0^2-\lambda_0\lambda_\ell+\lambda_\ell^2)/(\lambda_0^2\lambda_\ell^2)>0\). The inspected exact formal-series checker was independently replayed across positive and mixed-sign cases and agrees with the symbolic proof.

final_claim: For an interval with independent finite nonzero real Robin parameters \(\lambda_0,\lambda_\ell\), the zero eigenvalue occurs exactly on \(\ell=\lambda_0^{-1}+\lambda_\ell^{-1}\); the secular zero at \(k=0\) has order three on this resonance surface and order one otherwise, while the zero-energy scattering multiplicity is always one, so \(g_0-N/2=-1/2\) throughout the family.
limitations: Both Robin parameters are finite, real, and nonzero; Dirichlet/Neumann limits and non-self-adjoint conditions are excluded.
The contribution is the complete asymmetric one-edge anomaly classification, not a general quantum-graph theorem.
